statement: The f03 project-tie schema puts NativeMode/EnforcerScope/NativeTool/NativeTie in crates/enforcer-config/src/project_tie.rs and the declarative owner/exempt-glob/allow-regex/rule-toggle surface in a separate src/policy.rs, both new files inside the existing arc-03 enforcer-config crate (no new crate). ResolvedProjectTie::resolve() is the one entry point that produces a total, validated view: every recognized NativeTool always resolves to a ResolvedNativeTie (default Augment/Scoped), and Policy::validate() is run before the resolve succeeds.
why: f01 (MCP scan), f05 (native-tie step), and c04 (deny-hook) need a single resolved, total policy object rather than raw JSON or Option-soup, and the crate's existing resolve.rs/model.rs pattern (parse raw JSON -> typed struct -> total EffectiveConfig) was the established convention to match.
howToApply: Consumers should call enforcer_config::load_project_tie(path) or enforcer_config::parse_project_tie(raw, source_path) to get a ResolvedProjectTie, then call .tie(NativeTool::X) for a per-tool decision and read .policy for the declarative overrides. Never construct ProjectConfig/Policy directly from untrusted JSON outside this module.

statement: Disabling a rule via Policy.rule_toggles requires enabled=false AND a non-empty Waiver{ruleId,owner,reason} whose ruleId matches the map key; Policy::validate() rejects enabled=false with waiver=None, an empty owner/reason, or a mismatched waiver.ruleId, all as a ConfigLoadError::Parse at the .enforce/config load boundary (see parse_project_tie). This is deliberate: it makes rule suppression a committed, attributable, reviewable line of data instead of a silent flag flip.
why: The workpack's honesty-doctrine requirement bans silent/inline rule suppression; encoding the owner+reason requirement as a boundary-time validation (not just documentation) means a malformed or anonymous waiver fails the whole config load loudly, matching the existing crate convention of promoting former runtime findings to typed load-time errors.
howToApply: When c04 or f05 need to check whether a rule actually runs, call ResolvedProjectTie.policy.is_rule_enabled(&rule_id) rather than inspecting rule_toggles directly — absence of a toggle entry always means enabled, matching the 'never silently disabled by omission' invariant.

statement: enforcer-domain has no barrel re-exports (crates/enforcer-domain/src/lib.rs only does `pub mod ids; pub mod severity; ...`, no `pub use`), so RuleId and Severity must be referenced as enforcer_domain::ids::RuleId and enforcer_domain::severity::Severity, not enforcer_domain::RuleId. Also, this workspace denies clippy::unwrap_used and clippy::expect_used globally (see root Cargo.toml [workspace.lints.clippy]), so test helpers that construct known-valid branded newtypes (e.g. a RuleId from a literal) must return Result and propagate via `?` in `-> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>>` tests rather than calling .unwrap()/.expect().
why: Both are easy first-build compile/clippy failures for any new f0x/c0x lane touching enforcer-domain newtypes; worth recording so the next lane doesn't rediscover it via a failed cargo build.
howToApply: Import enforcer_domain types via their full module path (ids::/severity::/paths::/hashes::/findings::/records::/run_record::), and write any test needing a branded-newtype fixture as `fn test_name() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> { let x = Type::from_str("...")?; ... Ok(()) }`.

evidence.ref: cargo clippy -p enforcer-config --all-targets -- -D warnings; expect_used at policy.rs:163 before fix
